seeded_failure.symptom: Python application throws connection refused errors when attempting to connect to PostgreSQL on localhost port 5432.
seeded_failure.cause: The trainer started the PostgreSQL container mapped to host port 5433 instead of port 5432.
seeded_failure.fix: Identify port mismatch via docker ps and update the connection string port parameter to 5433 or restart container on port 5432.

lab_rubric: Database container setup
PostgreSQL container runs cleanly with persistent volumes, custom credentials, and published host ports.
PostgreSQL container runs in Docker and accepts external incoming connections.
PostgreSQL container runs but port mapping or persistence is misconfigured.
PostgreSQL container fails to start or run.
Python project configuration
Git repository structured cleanly with virtual environment, pinned requirements file, and verified connection script.
Git repository created with a virtual environment and working database query script.
Python script connects to database but lacks virtual environment isolation or Git tracking.
Python environment or database connectivity script is missing.
Data flow architecture diagram
Data flow diagram clearly identifies source formats, ingestion triggers, storage layers, and reporting tables.
Data flow diagram correctly labels sources, storage, transformations, and outputs.
Diagram is drawn but misses critical components like transformation steps or storage types.
Data flow diagram was not produced.
Troubleshooting the seeded failure
Identifies host port mismatch independently using Docker CLI commands and corrects configuration promptly.
Fixes connection error after reviewing container port mappings with a minor hint.
Diagnoses connection failure symptom but cannot resolve configuration cause.
Does not attempt troubleshooting.
